# Importing an Existing Setup

If you already have a hand-built `~/.claude/`, `~/.opencode/`, or `~/.codex/` directory, `cascade import` migrates it into Cascade's `.cascade/` tier structure without destroying anything.

---

## How it works

The import engine reads your existing files, maps each one to the appropriate Cascade tier, builds a coverage ledger that accounts for every byte, runs a round-trip verification, and only then writes anything. It refuses to apply the migration if the ledger reports any gap.

The process has three stages:

1. **Plan** — the engine walks the source directory, classifies files by type (instructions, memory, settings, inbox, etc.), and maps them to cascade tiers.
2. **Verify** — it reconstructs what the Cascade representation would look like and diffs it against the original. The round-trip must be lossless.
3. **Apply** — only if both previous stages pass does it write files to `.cascade/`.

Default mode is dry-run: it prints the plan and ledger without writing anything.

---

## Basic usage

```sh
# Dry-run (default): see the plan and coverage ledger
cascade import

# Specify a source directory
cascade import --from ~/.claude

# Specify the source harness
cascade import --harness opencode

# Apply the migration (writes files, only if lossless)
cascade import --apply

# Emit the plan as JSON (useful in CI)
cascade import --report-json
```

---

## Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--from <PATH>` | `-f` | Source directory. Auto-detects `~/.claude`, `~/.opencode`, `~/.codex` if omitted. |
| `--harness <NAME>` | | Source harness: `claude-code` (default), `opencode`, `codex`. |
| `--dest <PATH>` | `-d` | Destination `.cascade/` directory. Defaults to `<cwd>/.cascade/`. |
| `--apply` | `-a` | Write files. Refused if the coverage ledger reports any gap. |
| `--report-json` | | Emit the full plan or report as JSON to stdout. |

---

## Reading the coverage ledger

When you run `cascade import` without `--apply`, the output includes a coverage ledger table. Each row is one source file. The status column tells you what happened:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mapped` | File maps cleanly to a Cascade tier. Will be written on `--apply`. |
| `merged` | File's content merged into an existing tier file. |
| `skipped` | File is a derived output (e.g. `CLAUDE.md` generated by Cascade) and is not imported. |
| `gap` | File could not be mapped. The import will not proceed until this is resolved. |

If any row shows `gap`, the final line reads `NOT LOSSLESS — apply refused`. Fix the gap (usually by specifying `--harness` if the tool was misdetected) and re-run.

---

## Supported source harnesses

| Harness | Source directory | Files imported |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-code` | `~/.claude/` | `CLAUDE.md` (GCI instructions), `settings.json`, `memory/`, `inbox/`, `projects/` |
| `opencode` | `~/.opencode/` | `opencode.json`, per-project instruction files |
| `codex` | `~/.codex/` | `config.json`, per-project context files |

---

## What happens to the original files

Nothing. `cascade import --apply` only writes to the `.cascade/` destination. It does not move, delete, or modify the source directory. Your existing tool setup continues to work exactly as before.

If you want to switch fully to Cascade-managed files, run `cascade generate-instructions` after import to regenerate derived files from the cascade hierarchy. Your old `.claude/CLAUDE.md` becomes a file Cascade generates from the cascade hierarchy rather than one you maintain manually.

---

## Difference from `cascade migrate`

`cascade migrate` is a simpler file-move tool: it copies files from a legacy directory to `.cascade/` without a coverage ledger or round-trip verification. Use `cascade import` when you want a proven lossless migration. Use `cascade migrate` for a quick move where you are comfortable reviewing the result manually.

---

## Troubleshooting

**`NOT LOSSLESS — apply refused`**
The coverage ledger found at least one file it could not map. Run with `--report-json` to see the full gap list, then check whether `--harness` matches your source tool.

**`auto-detect found nothing`**
None of `~/.claude`, `~/.opencode`, or `~/.codex` exist. Pass `--from <path>` to point at your directory.

**`destination already has files`**
`cascade import --apply` will not overwrite existing `.cascade/` files. If you want to re-run from scratch, rename or remove the existing `.cascade/` directory first, or specify a different `--dest`.
